topic: Should you exercise after a massage?

slides.headline: Gym after a massage: yes or no?
slides.sub: It depends on the session and what you're training.

slides.title: Light movement: usually yes
slides.body: A walk, easy cycling or your physio exercises after a massage is generally fine and can help you enjoy that looser feeling. Gentle movement is a good habit here.

slides.title: Heavy or explosive: maybe wait
slides.body: After deep work on a muscle group, some people feel a bit heavy or less springy for a few hours. Many save max lifts, sprints or races for the next day.

slides.title: Plan around big sessions
slides.body: Got a key session this week? Book your massage after it, or a day or two before. That way you're recovering, not testing legs that feel a little different.

slides.title: Check in the next morning
slides.body: Feeling tender for a day is common after firm work. If a spot is still sore when you warm up, drop the intensity and give it another day before going hard.

slides.title: Massage supports, training builds
slides.body: Massage complements active rehab rather than replacing it. Strength and conditioning are still what build capacity over time, so keep your usual training going with sensible timing.

slides.headline: Book your massage around training
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists ask about your training week and tailor pressure and timing to suit. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Massage today, training tonight: good idea or not?

Light movement after a massage is usually fine and can feel great. A walk, an easy spin or your rehab exercises are all reasonable. Heavy lifting, sprints or a race are a different story: after deep work, some people feel heavy or flat for a few hours, so many save the big efforts for the next day.

If you have a key session or event coming up in the new year, book your massage after it or a day or two before. Massage supports your recovery, while training is still what builds capacity.
